Hi @jsturtevant, I promoted a WS 2019 node to be the domain controller by using the upstream script https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/windows-testing/blob/master/extensions/gmsa-dc/v1/Promote-DC.ps1. In this way, I got the same DC used in upstream testing right? I tested this pr against this DC and failed to access the resource by domain name.

Is your DNS configured on the node and pod?  can you do Resolve-DnsName <domain> from both?  You need to set the [DNS of the worker nodes](https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/windows-testing/blob/9cfbfb7c9e91190abe91c649ee9ad3b13274457d/extensions/gmsa-member/v1/Join-Domain.ps1#L47-L49) and the [pods need to have DNS configured to the see the domain](https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/windows-testing/blob/master/extensions/gmsa-coredns/v1/update-coredns.sh#L12-L33).

You also need to make sure the GMSACredentialSpec `DomainJoinConfig.DnsName` is using the fqdn domain name (which I think it is by default).

> GMSACredentialSpec

### What would you like to be added?

1. "work e2e" and "read/write file" test cases have the same set up and clean up functions. We should hoist the same setup logic to a beforeEach and do the clean up in a afterEach. Create this issue to track it as mentioned in this comment: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/108432#discussion_r819055340

2. Follow up on using dns name in the remote folder path instead of ip. (mentioned in this comment: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/108432#discussion_r824879707)
### Why is this needed?

To remove the redundant code and make it clear and efficient.
